There is only one consclusion that can be reached; if future flooding of the area occurs, a large part of the resources committed under the scheduled rehabilitation activity will be irrevocably lost. This is "the primary major negative impact" that concerns the proposed project. It is to be discussed further in Part VI covering adverse environmental effects which cannot be avoided.
b. New Construction
New construction and redevelopment within the area of the 100 year flood would be subject to floods of a 100 year frequency if the proposed flood pkain ordinances were not adopted. However, because they must be adopted and enforced as a condition of the urban renewal project and because project land will not be disposed of for redevelopment until such ordinances are adopted, with proper code enforcement new construction will be protected from floods of 100 year frequency.
c. Public Improvements
Future flooding will cause some damage to public improvements placed there as a result of the project. This damage is not expected to be extensive, judging from the type and amount of damage caused by the most recent flood.
Commitment of resources, in this case, is considered to have only a minor negative impact.
